summary:
**SARVIA Neza: A 3D Digital Twin for Ground Subsidence**

SARVIA Neza is a 3D digital twin designed to help understand and visualize ground subsidence in Nezahualcóyotl, Mexico, a city facing serious land sinking problems. This movement can damage streets, buildings, and water pipes, putting thousands of people at risk.

Our project combines NASA’s NISAR satellite radar data with terrain information, roads, and buildings to create an interactive 3D view of the city. Users can explore areas affected by ground movement, identify streets and buildings exposed to these changes, and simulate different scenarios using an interactive slider.

SARVIA Neza turns satellite data into clear and useful information for local authorities. It can help the Nezahualcóyotl City Council identify areas that need closer inspection, prioritize infrastructure maintenance, and make better decisions about public resources. Our goal is to make space data easier to understand and use, supporting safer neighborhoods and more informed urban planning.
details:
Project Details – SARVIA Neza

SARVIA Neza is an interactive 3D digital twin that helps people understand ground subsidence in Nezahualcóyotl, Mexico. The project aims to turn satellite data into clear information that can support better decisions about urban infrastructure.

The project works in three main steps. First, it uses NASA’s NISAR radar data to observe ground movement over time. Second, it combines this information with terrain data from Copernicus DEM and city infrastructure, such as roads and buildings, to create a 3D view of the affected areas. Finally, users can explore different zones, identify streets and buildings exposed to ground movement, and use an interactive slider to simulate possible scenarios.

One of the main benefits of SARVIA Neza is that it makes complex satellite information easier to understand. Instead of only showing data on a map, it allows users to explore the city in 3D and see how ground movement may affect urban areas. This can help local authorities, especially the Nezahualcóyotl City Council, prioritize inspections, plan infrastructure maintenance, and use public resources more efficiently.

Our project is creative because it combines satellite observations, city infrastructure, 3D visualization, and interactive simulation in a single tool. It connects information from space with real urban challenges at street level.

We considered the importance of data quality, the needs of local authorities, the impact on communities, and the difference between exposure and actual damage. Our simulations are designed to explore possible scenarios, not to predict future damage.

SARVIA Neza uses NASA NISAR L2 GUNW data from October 25, 2025, to January 17, 2026, along with Copernicus DEM, roads, and buildings. Our goal is to support safer neighborhoods through better access to satellite-based information. In the future, the project could be improved with more satellite observations, local data validation, and expanded to other cities facing ground subsidence.
